(Justification: The paper is a non-review research article that explicitly implements national-scale (Cambodia) spatial land system modeling to predict future land use/land cover (LULC) change up to 2040. Its primary objective is to evaluate how alternative large-scale land acquisition (LSLA) governance policies affect future LULC patterns, particularly tree cover and natural areas. It develops and quantitatively compares three distinct future policy scenarios using the CLUMondo land system change model. The modeling is spatially explicit at 1 km resolution, includes mapped LULC projections (Fig. 1–3), and reports quantitative outputs such as area changes in land systems, tree cover (Tables 3–5), and core natural area metrics. Although tiger reintroduction is a conservation motivation, LULC prediction is the central method and focus—not a secondary input—and the ecological assessment is derived directly from the modeled LULC outcomes. The study meets all core inclusion criteria and avoids all exclusion criteria.)
